== 70% ==
Answer the question below.

John writes with his right hand and the last word he’d write if he was writing this sentence would be '''be'''.<br>If Keith writes with his left hand, what would be the last word he would write in the sentence above?

It doesn’t matter if you’re right-handed or left-handed, the last word in the first sentence is always ‘be’.

== 30% ==
Jamil is writing a limerick but needs a word that follows these rules to complete the last line…

Two syllables, only two different vowels, starts with an even-numbered letter and contains at least three letters from the second half of the alphabet.
{| class="fandom-table"
! colspan="5" |Which of these words would work?
|-
|DOGGIE
|BLAZES
|HOTEL
|'''PRIZES'''
|RABBIT
|}
DOGGIE has three vowels, BLAZES, HOTEL and RABBIT only have two letters from the second half of the alphabet (N-Z).

The letters represent the first letter of their positions within the boxes – '''U'''P, '''D'''OWN, '''L'''EFT and then '''R''' for '''R'''IGHT.

== 20% ==
What number replaces the question mark below?

E – 1 = F<Br>W – 2 = V<Br>Q – 1 = O<Br>H – 2 = I<Br>E - '''2''' = L

The number refers to the number of lines that get removed from the first letter to make the second letter.
